title: Smash Burger Tacos with Special Sauce
changes_from_base: Same 60 g balls and screaming-hot pan as the Classic, but each ball is smashed with a tortilla laid on top, so meat and tortilla fuse into one crisp taco. No buns; cheese goes on after the flip and the taco is folded.
summary: Smash-burger beef is pressed thin directly onto a tortilla so the two fuse into one crisp-edged wrap, then folded up with a tangy homemade burger sauce.
equipment: large cast-iron or heavy steel frying pan (at least 26 cm) or flat griddle
stiff metal spatula (fish slice or burger turner)

ingredients.note: about 40 g each; check the label for lard if keeping halal

ingredients.item: dill pickles, finely chopped, plus 1 tbsp of their brine

steps.title: Mix the special sauce
steps.text: Stir together the mayonnaise, ketchup, finely chopped pickles with their tablespoon of brine, mustard, garlic powder and paprika in a small bowl. Chill it while you prepare everything else so the flavours have a few minutes to settle and mellow. The pickle brine adds a tangy backbone that plain pickles alone wouldn't give the sauce.

steps.title: Prep the lettuce and onion
steps.text: Shred the lettuce and finely chop the onion, then set both aside ready to fold in later. Doing this now means you can move quickly once the beef is cooking, since each taco needs building and folding while the tortilla is still hot and pliable.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Place a dry cast-iron or steel pan over high heat for 4-5 minutes until a flicked drop of water skitters and disappears instantly. This intense, dry heat lets the thin beef caramelise into a crisp crust in the couple of minutes it spends in the pan, rather than just warming through.

steps.title: Season and top with a tortilla
steps.text: Season a beef ball lightly all over with salt and pepper, then lower it into the hot pan, working with 2 at a time to match the tortilla size. Lay a tortilla directly on top of each ball so it sits centred over the meat, ready for pressing.

steps.title: Smash through the tortilla
steps.text: Press down hard on the tortilla with a spatula, using your weight, until the beef spreads out almost to the tortilla's edge and thins to around 5mm. Do this firmly within the first 20-30 seconds so the meat bonds properly to the tortilla as it cooks - a timid press leaves the two separating later when you pick it up.

steps.title: Sear until lacy
steps.text: Leave the beef-topped tortillas undisturbed for 2-2.5 minutes until the edges of the meat turn deeply brown and lacy. This hard, direct contact with the pan builds the crust; disturbing it early stops that crust forming properly.

steps.title: Flip and melt the cheese
steps.text: Scrape underneath firmly to lift the whole crust, then flip so the tortilla is now against the pan. Lay half a slice of cheese on the beef and cook for 60-90 seconds more, until the tortilla is crisp and spotted brown and the beef reaches 71°C with no pink left.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Lift each taco out and spoon over the special sauce, then scatter on lettuce, onion and a few sesame seeds before folding the tortilla over the filling. Serve 2 tacos per person while the tortilla is still crisp at the edges and warm through the middle.

tips: Press firmly and early so the meat properly bonds to the tortilla - a light press will leave the beef sliding off when you pick the taco up.
If your tortillas feel stiff, warm them for about 10 seconds first so they don't crack under the spatula.
Don't overfill - a modest spoonful of sauce and a light scatter of lettuce fold much more neatly than a heaped one.
Cook only as many as will fit without crowding, since the tortilla needs full contact with the pan to crisp evenly.
storage: These are best eaten straight from the pan while the tortilla is crisp. Leftover cooked beef (without the tortilla) keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days or frozen for up to 2 months; reheat in a hot pan until piping hot and 74°C at the centre, then fold into a fresh tortilla with the sauce and salad.
